items.prompt: Black has played ...e5. Tap every hole in Black's pawn structure: a square on the fourth, fifth or sixth rank that no black pawn attacks now or can attack by advancing.

claims.statement: b6 and d5 are the holes: no black pawn can ever attack them.

hints: A hole is a square that Black's pawns cannot cover. Which black pawns are still able to move forward and attack something?
Look at the squares in front of the pawns on a6, b7 and d6. Which of them are never attacked by a pawn?
One of the holes is the square in front of the d6 pawn; the other is on the queen side.
items.explain: A hole needs two things: no black pawn attacks it now, and none can reach a square from which it would. The pawn on a6 cannot attack b6 (it only attacks b5) and the pawn on c7 is gone, so b6 is a hole; the pawn on d6 has no neighbour on c7 or e7 to attack d5, so d5 is a hole. These are facts about the pawns only; whether the hole matters depends on the pieces.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap the one empty square where a white knight would be defended by a pawn and that no black pawn can ever attack.

claims.statement: d5 is the only empty outpost square for White.

hints: The square must be defended by a white pawn. Which white pawn stands next to the black territory?
The pawn on e4 defends two squares in front of it. One of them is empty and has no black pawn beside it.
It is on the d-file, in front of Black's backward pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on e4 defends d5. The black pawns on d6 and e5 are past it, and Black has no c-pawn and no e6 pawn that could attack d5, so no pawn can ever chase a knight from there. That is an outpost.
